title: Multilingual Homogeneity: Are Shared Blind Spots Worse in Low-Resource Languages?

original_idea.body:
# Multilingual Homogeneity: Are Shared Blind Spots Worse in Low-Resource Languages?

**Problem:** Success state: deployers in non-English markets know whether model homogeneity (and its safety blind spots) is amplified in their language. Backward: the Hivemind study is English-centric; we need to know if convergence and correlated safety failures intensify in lower-resource languages.

**Direction:** Translate a fixed set of open-ended and safety-relevant prompts into 3-4 languages of varying resource levels. Measure inter-model output homogeneity and shared refusal blind spots per language across several multilingual open models. Test whether lower-resource languages show higher convergence and more universal safety failures.

**Why it matters:** If homogeneity worsens in under-resourced languages, billions of users get both more uniform thought and more correlated safety holes, while these populations are least covered by lab red-teaming — a neglected, diffuse, medium-horizon risk ideal for counterfactual work.

**Relevant context:** Extends Artificial Hivemind cross-model homogeneity to multilingual settings. Open multilingual models (Qwen, Gemma, Aya-style) run on one GPU; uses public/translated prompts.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: amplified correlated safety failures in low-resource languages affect billions least covered by red-teaming; defensible neglected harm.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: translate prompts + measure per-language homogeneity; translation quality is the main wrinkle.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (homogeneity vs language resource level) with translation as dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected multilingual angle, open models, inference-only; weak lab incentive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference over translated prompt set on open models; minimal compute.

novelty.reasoning: English-centric homogeneity shown; multilingual extension may be open (overlaps gen-1202).

novelty_assessment.reasoning: English homogeneity shown; multilingual extension partially open.
